title: Units and Picard groups of the line and the punctured line
statement:
Let $k$ be a field. On the
small etale site of the
smooth separated curves
$\mathbf A^1_k=\Spec k[T]$ and $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\Spec k[T,T^{-1}]$ over
$k$, the unit sheaf $\mathbf G_m$
satisfies

$$
\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_k,\mathbf G_m)=k^\times,\qquad
\Gamma(\mathbf G_{m,k},\mathbf G_m)=k^\times\cdot t^{\mathbf Z},
$$

and, in the notation of [def-sc-picard-group],

$$
\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbf A^1_k)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbf G_{m,k})=0.
$$

Moreover, for every $N\geq1$ prime to $\operatorname{char}k$,
the $N$-power map on $\Gamma(\mathbf G_{m,k},\mathbf G_m)$ has cokernel
$k^\times/(k^\times)^N\oplus\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$.
If every element of $k^\times$ is an $N$-th power (e.g. if $k$
is algebraically closed), this cokernel is generated by the class of
$t$, and the $N$-power map on $k^\times$ is surjective.

proof.text: By definition the unit sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ has $\mathbf G_m(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$ (Stacks Tag 03P4, etale-cohomology-definition-additive-sheaf (2)). In particular its global sections are its value on the terminal object $X\to X$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], for $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ this is $R^\times$. Thus the two section groups in the statement are respectively $k[T]^\times$ and $k[T,T^{-1}]^\times$. This uses only the defining value of the unit sheaf, not an etale cohomology comparison.

Use Polynomial.isUnit_iff to identify each polynomial unit with a scalar unit. Polynomial.C_injective gives uniqueness. Compose this bijection with the canonical equivalence from coordinate-ring units to global etale unit sections.

source.place: Proof, computation of the units of k[T]

proof.text: For a Laurent unit u, LaurentPolynomial.exists_T_pow writes u*T^n as the image of a polynomial p. Its image is a unit. The localization unit criterion says p divides a power of X; primality of X implies p is associated to X^i. Polynomial.isUnit_iff identifies the associated unit with a scalar a, giving u=a*T^(i-n). Conversely every such monomial is a unit. Equality of Laurent degrees forces equality of the exponents, and multiplication by the inverse of T^n followed by comparison of coefficient zero forces equality of the scalars. This gives the multiplicative coordinate equivalence.

source.place: Proof, computation of Laurent units, with the extreme-exponent argument written out

proof.text: Infer the principal ideal domain structure on k[T] using lem-pur-polynomial-field-pid. For an ideal J of the Laurent ring, take the principal contracted ideal in k[T]. Mapping its generator gives a principal ideal, and IsLocalization.map_under identifies that mapped ideal with J. LaurentPolynomial already supplies the integral-domain instance.

source.place: Proof, opening assertion that both coordinate rings are principal ideal domains; localization argument expanded

proof.text: The current [lem-sc-affine-invertible-sections] statement says directly that, for an affine open, the section module is invertible and its canonical evaluation map is bijective. Let $R$ be either coordinate ring and let $\mathcal L$ be an arbitrary invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module on $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Apply that statement with the affine open $U=X$: for $M=\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\otimes_R M\to R$, $\varphi\otimes m\mapsto\varphi(m)$, is bijective. Step 4 verifies precisely the domain and principal-ideal hypotheses of [lem-pur-pid-invertible-module-trivial], which gives $M\cong R$ as $R$-modules. Neither finite generation nor projectivity is being assumed without justification: the cited module theorem has exactly the evaluation-map hypothesis supplied by the affine-sections theorem.

source.place: Tag 0BCH, lemma-UFD-Pic-trivial (rank-one consequence over a PID); affine-section input from the existing project theorem

proof.text: Use the existing free-generator API in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.InvertibleSections: isFreeGenerator_of_bijective_smul turns the basis of global sections from step 5 into a sheaf free generator on the affine top open. Compare with the generator 1 of the unit sheaf using nonempty_iso_of_isFreeGenerator on the singleton cover by the top open. Equality of the two restricted scalar coefficients follows from injectivity for the generator, so the transition compatibility is immediate. Thus every invertible sheaf is isomorphic to the unit sheaf. Scheme.Pic.eq_iff_nonempty_iso then identifies any two Picard classes, proving both vanishings. This avoids an explicit tilde/Gamma counit in this proof.

source.place: Tags 01IA and 01IB, lemma-quasi-coherent-affine and lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent; Picard convention Tag 040C

proof.text: Under the unique decomposition of step 3 the $N$-power map is $(\alpha,m)\mapsto(\alpha^N,Nm)$. Define $q(\alpha t^m)=([\alpha],[m])$ in $k^\times/(k^\times)^N\oplus\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$. This is a surjective group homomorphism: representatives of the two classes give a preimage. Its kernel consists precisely of $\alpha=\beta^N$ and $m=Nn$, equivalently $\alpha t^m=(\beta t^n)^N$. Hence $q$ identifies two units exactly when their ratio is an $N$-th power, and induces a bijective homomorphism from the cokernel onto the asserted direct sum. Its inverse sends $([\alpha],[m])$ to the class of $\alpha t^m$; if $\alpha'=\alpha\beta^N$ and $m'=m+Nn$, then $(\alpha't^{m'})/(\alpha t^m)=(\beta t^n)^N$, so the inverse is independent of both representatives. This also checks directly that no quotient or product compatibility is left implicit.

source.place: Proof, product decomposition and the two cokernels

proof.text: If every element of $k^\times$ is an $N$-th power, the first summand in step 7 is trivial, and the remaining group $\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$ is generated by $[1]$, the image of $t$. The same hypothesis is exactly surjectivity of the power map on $k^\times$. For algebraically closed $k$ and $a\ne0$, a root $b$ of $X^N-a$ exists by algebraic closedness and satisfies $b\ne0$, so $a=b^N$. For $N=1$ the cokernel is zero and the class of $t$ is its (trivial) generator. The characteristic restriction is retained as stated, although none of these algebraic computations needs it.

source.place: Proof, final sentence and the N=1 edge case

proof_origin.place: Proof, formalized by A8 using polynomial localization for Laurent units and ideals, existing affine invertible-section/free-generator theorems for Picard vanishing, and the explicit coordinate homomorphism and its kernel for the cokernel. Mathlib supplies polynomial units, PID Picard triviality and the quotient first isomorphism theorem.
